title: fix(test): test_phi_block_via_mock_provider depends on undocumented mock_mode and has wrong assertion
description: proxy/tests/test_chat.py:82-92: test relies on settings.mock_mode=True in the environment (never set by the fixture). If mock_mode=False the request raises 400 and assert 'error' in resp_body passes anyway, masking failure. Fix: explicitly patch settings.mock_mode=True in the fixture and add assert response.status_code == 403.

title: fix(deploy): no Fly.io migration step in deploy pipeline
description: The migrate service exists only in docker-compose.yml. make deploy ships governance to Fly.io without running alembic upgrade head first. Production deployments of governance start against an unmigrated schema on first deploy or any schema-adding migration. Add a migration step to the Makefile deploy target (fly ssh console or a release_command in fly-governance.toml).

title: fix(perf): bcrypt calls block async event loop in auth and create_key
description: proxy/app/auth.py:32,49 calls bcrypt.checkpw() synchronously on every API-key authenticated request. proxy/app/main.py:373 calls bcrypt.hashpw() on key creation. Each bcrypt call at cost-12 takes 100-300ms and freezes all in-flight requests. Wrap every bcrypt call in asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(None, ...).

title: fix(api): block response uses JSONResponse while all other errors use HTTPException
description: proxy/app/main.py:244-254: policy block returns JSONResponse(content=error_envelope()) giving shape {error:{}} while every HTTPException path gives {detail:{error:{}}}. Clients need two error parsers. Standardize all error responses to one shape — recommend HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=error_envelope(...)) everywhere.

title: fix(security): delete_user proxy hardcodes 202 — silent GDPR erasure failure
description: proxy/app/main.py:407 hardcodes status_code=202 regardless of governance response. A failed GDPR erasure (governance 404/500) reports success to the admin. Fix: use resp.status_code instead of hardcoded 202.

title: fix(security): _me_cache key collision enables cross-tenant data leak
description: The _me_cache TTLCache in proxy/app/main.py:333 uses only caller.user_id as the cache key. Admin-assigned string user IDs from different tenants can collide, serving tenant A's allowed_models/roles/rate-limit config to tenant B's user. Fix: change cache_key to (caller.tenant_id, caller.user_id).

title: fix: comprehensive review remediation — security, performance, correctness, deployment
description: Address all 35 findings from the exhaustive multi-agent code review of feat/ai-gateway-1lo. Covers 6 critical, 19 important, and 10 nice-to-have issues spanning security (cross-tenant cache, GDPR silent failure, JWT), performance (bcrypt blocking event loop, missing indexes), correctness (asymmetric response shape, UUID7, settings), and deployment (no Fly.io migration step, OPA image divergence).

title: fix(resource): provision.py DB connection leaks on exception — no try/finally
description: scripts/provision.py:53: conn = psycopg2.connect(db_url) is called but conn.close() at line 193 is only reached on the happy path. Any exception during provisioning leaks the DB connection. Fix: wrap the entire body in try/finally: conn.close() or use contextlib.closing(psycopg2.connect(db_url)).

title: fix(audit): audit_id returned in response before background write completes — phantom IDs possible
description: governance/app/main.py:123-134: audit_id is in the HTTP response but the DB write is a BackgroundTask. If write fails (only logged to stderr), the returned ID is phantom — no corresponding audit_log row. Fix: at minimum add a dead-letter table for failed audit writes and expose a metric on audit write failure rate.

title: fix(deploy): Dockerfile.proxy bakes config/ into image diverging from volume-mounted local
description: Dockerfile.proxy (used by Fly.io) includes COPY config/ config/ embedding model routing config at build time. docker-compose.yml mounts it as a volume at runtime. Config changes require full image rebuild on Fly.io but are hot-reloadable locally. Document this tradeoff or switch Fly.io to an external config volume/env-var approach.

title: fix(deploy): OPA image tag divergence between local and production
description: docker-compose.yml uses openpolicyagent/opa:latest-static; fly-opa.toml uses openpolicyagent/opa:latest-rootless. Different variants and both float on latest. A breaking OPA release breaks production without breaking local. Fix: pin both to the same explicit semver tag e.g. openpolicyagent/opa:0.68.0-static and openpolicyagent/opa:0.68.0-rootless.

title: fix(security): PSEUDONYM_HMAC_KEY unnecessarily exposed to cron machine
description: fly-cron.toml and fly-secrets.sh.example set PSEUDONYM_HMAC_KEY on the cron machine. rotate_partitions.py only reads DATABASE_URL — it never uses PSEUDONYM_HMAC_KEY. Violates least-privilege. Fix: remove PSEUDONYM_HMAC_KEY from the cron app secrets and the fly-cron.toml comment.

title: fix(deploy): partial Fly.io deploy failure leaves governance/proxy version skew with no rollback
description: Makefile:54-57: if fly deploy fly-governance.toml succeeds but fly.toml fails, new governance is live with old proxy. If governance API changed shape all traffic breaks. Fix: add --strategy=rolling --wait-timeout=120 to each deploy call. Consider versioning the internal /inspect endpoint as /v1/inspect to allow graceful rollback.

title: fix(security): JWT tokens have no expiry or audience validation
description: proxy/app/auth.py: jwt.decode() is called without requiring exp or aud claims. python-jose validates exp if present but does not require it — a JWT without exp is valid forever. Fix: add options={'require': ['exp']} and validate aud='ai-gateway'. Ensure all token issuance includes exp (e.g., 1 hour TTL).

title: fix(settings): governance uses Pydantic v1 Config class in pydantic-settings v2 project
description: governance/app/settings.py:16-17 uses 'class Config: env_file = .env' which is Pydantic v1 syntax. The proxy correctly uses model_config = {'env_file': '.env'} (pydantic-settings v2 style). Fix: replace with model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env') to be consistent and avoid deprecation warnings.

title: fix(correctness): UUID7 implementation uses non-standard bit extraction
description: governance/app/audit.py:17-24: rand_a = (rand >> 62) & 0xFFF on an 80-bit value takes bits 73-62, which overlaps conceptually with rand_b's range and wastes randomness. UUIDs produced have correct version/variant but the extraction is opaque and non-spec-compliant. Fix: use the uuid6 library (pip package) instead of the hand-rolled implementation.

title: fix(opa): OPA 4xx responses escape OPAError hierarchy and log as unexpected exception
description: governance/app/opa.py:48-52: resp.raise_for_status() raises httpx.HTTPStatusError which is not caught in the try block. Falls through to BaseException branch in pipeline.py (still fail-closed, no security bypass) but logged as 'unexpected OPA exception' making OPA 400s undetectable. Fix: add except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc: raise OPAResultError(...) from exc.

title: fix(perf): missing database indexes cause full partition scans
description: governance/migrations: no index on audit_log(tenant_id, created_at DESC) for audit_list queries; no index on audit_log(user_id) for GDPR erasure; PK is (audit_id, created_at) but export keyset queries ORDER BY created_at, audit_id — wrong column order; no partial index on user_pseudonym_map WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Add a new Alembic migration with these four indexes.

title: fix(resource): OPA httpx.AsyncClient is module-level global that is never closed
description: governance/app/opa.py:27-34: the httpx.AsyncClient is lazily created and stored as a module global, never closed in the lifespan teardown. Leaks connections on shutdown and in tests. Fix: move creation into the governance lifespan, store on app.state, pass to check() as a parameter — same pattern used by the proxy.

title: fix(concurrency): harm scanner lazy-init has thread-safety race under asyncio.to_thread
description: governance/app/harm.py:13-21: harm_scan is called via asyncio.to_thread. Two concurrent requests can both see _injection_scanner is None and race to initialize ML models. A partially-constructed scanner returns blocked=False (fail-open for harm scanning). Fix: initialize both scanners in the lifespan startup or add threading.Lock around the lazy-init check.

title: fix(health): governance health endpoint resolves DB session before _ready=True
description: governance/app/main.py:68-78: FastAPI resolves Depends(get_session) before the handler body. During startup (_ready=False) if DB is not ready, get_session fails with connection error returning 500 instead of 503. Load balancers interpret 500 as unhealthy and may restart prematurely. Fix: move _ready check before the DB dependency is involved, or separate the health endpoint into two: /health/ready and /health/live.

title: fix(gdpr): erasure_id returned to caller but never persisted in erasure_log
description: governance/app/main.py:314: erasure_id is generated and returned in the response but the erasure_log INSERT has no erasure_id column. The GDPR audit trail cannot be cross-referenced by the erasure ID. Fix: add erasure_id column to erasure_log table (new Alembic migration) and include it in the INSERT.

title: fix(audit): created_at and written_at are identical timestamps — semantic distinction lost
description: governance/app/audit.py:34-56: both created_at and written_at are set inside write_audit (which runs in the background task after the response is sent). The comment 'populated after processing' on written_at is false. Fix: pass created_at into write_audit from the inspect handler so it reflects the request-received time, not the write time.

title: fix(security): audit_list leaks all tenants records when tenant_id omitted
description: proxy/app/main.py:424-430 forwards dict(request.query_params) directly to governance. governance/app/main.py:246-258 uses WHERE (:tenant_id IS NULL OR tenant_id = :tenant_id) — omitting tenant_id returns ALL tenants records. Fix: always inject params={'tenant_id': caller.tenant_id} in the proxy audit endpoint, ignoring any caller-supplied tenant_id.

title: fix(security): create_key has no input validation and no tenant isolation
description: proxy/app/main.py:366-368: payload['user_id'] raises KeyError (→500) if missing. No enforcement that payload['tenant_id'] == caller.tenant_id — an admin in tenant A can issue keys for tenant B. Fix: add a Pydantic CreateKeyRequest model, validate required fields, and enforce tenant_id == caller.tenant_id.

title: fix(security): BodySizeLimitMiddleware bypassed by omitting Content-Length
description: proxy/app/main.py:110-115 and governance/app/main.py:54-62 only check the Content-Length header. Chunked-encoded requests omitting the header bypass the check entirely and request.json() reads the full body into memory. Pre-auth DoS vector. Fix: read and cap the streaming body directly in the middleware rather than trusting the header.

title: Phase 6: Deployment and Portfolio Polish
description: Fly.io deployment (proxy public, governance + opa internal-only), separate fly.toml per service, performance-1x for governance, auto_stop_machines, SPACY_MODEL switch (sm on Fly, lg locally), Fly secrets for all sensitive env, Fly scheduled job for rotate_partitions, README with Mermaid C4 diagrams + design rationale (no-LiteLLM, GDPR pseudonyms, RLS), docs/demo-scenarios.md, scripts/demo.sh and make demo target.
acceptance_criteria: make up && make demo runs all scenarios and prints pass/fail; governance cold-start <30s on Fly with en_core_web_sm; Fly demo URL reachable; README self-sufficient; pre-commit hook active; /docs disabled on Fly deployments.

title: Phase 1: Project Foundation
description: Bootstrap repo: monorepo layout, docker-compose with healthcheck chain (postgres/redis/opa/migrate/proxy/governance), Makefile, direnv, config YAMLs, idempotent provisioner, base FastAPI apps with /health, CORS + 1MB body-size middleware on both services.
acceptance_criteria: make up starts all services detached; make provision is idempotent and prints generated keys once; /health on both services returns 503 until ready then 200; OPA bundle loads and hot-reloads on policies/data/users.json change; bootstrap is idempotent (re-run does not create second admin via bootstrap_state row check); >1MB body rejected with 413.

title: Phase 3: Reference Proxy
description: OpenAI-compatible proxy: routes for /v1/chat/completions, /v1/models, /v1/me, admin /v1/keys, /v1/audit, /v1/audit/export, DELETE /v1/users/{id}. Auth (bcrypt + TTLCache + JWT HS256 pinned), Redis Lua rate limiter (atomic, retry_after return), 5-step provider resolution BEFORE /inspect, governance client with X-Internal-Token + tenacity + fail-closed, OpenAI-shape error envelopes + rate-limit and PII-redaction headers, mock provider for portfolio demos, match/case dispatch (no ABC).
acceptance_criteria: OpenAI Python SDK works against the proxy; bcrypt path validates keys; JWT HS256-pinned (none algorithm rejected); X-Gateway-Provider routing works only with gateway:provider_override:<name> permission (denied attempts emit routing_method=override_denied audit rows); GET /v1/models OPA-filtered; GET /v1/me returns user/tenant/roles/allowed_models/rate_limit/pii_policy; rate limit atomic with no over-admit; every response carries x-ratelimit-* headers; 429 carries both Retry-After and retry-after-ms; PII redaction emits X-Gateway-Pii-Redacted (suppressed for silent tenants); required_roles present in error body, current_roles never echoed; MOCK_PROVIDERS=true demos run without network; governance down -> 503 fail-closed; /docs disabled when DOCS_ENABLED=false; >1MB rejected with 413; unlisted origin blocked by CORS.

title: Phase 2: Governance Engine Core
description: Governance engine /inspect with X-Internal-Token, PII (Presidio singleton via asyncio.to_thread + asyncio.Lock), harm (llm-guard), OPA client (fail-closed, deny+allow check), middleware-style pipeline with PII-before-OPA ordering, HMAC-SHA256 pseudonymization, metadata-only audit log with written_at, UUIDv7 audit_id, native monthly RANGE partitions pre-created, RLS FORCED, INSERT-only role + mutation trigger, keyset-paginated JSONL export, GDPR erasure workflow.
acceptance_criteria: POST /inspect with valid token + clean prompt -> allow; missing token -> 403; PII -> redact with metadata-only findings (no matched text); jailbreak -> block; OPA deny+allow=true -> blocks (deny wins); audit_log.user_id is HMAC pseudonym; audit_id has UUIDv7 version nibble == 7; initial 3 monthly partitions exist and INSERT succeeds for current month; RLS denies with no session vars; checkout listener prevents session-var leak across pooled connections; written_at and routing_method populated; DELETE /v1/users/{id} writes erasure_log and overwrites real_user_id with [ERASED]; GET /v1/audit/export streams NDJSON with Link rel="next" cursor.

title: Phase 5: OPA Policies and Testing
description: Full Rego policy suite evaluating the RESOLVED provider: authz.rego (model access + data classification), audit_scope.rego (SELF|TENANT|PLATFORM mapping, default-deny on unknown role), provider_override.rego (per-provider permission), allow_model.rego (enumerate-and-filter, no partial eval). Test suite includes the critical deny+allow coexistence case.
acceptance_criteria: make opa-test green; PHI + non-approved provider + tier2 user yields allow=true AND deny non-empty (pipeline must block); tier2 model + non-tier2 role -> deny; per-provider override permission honored (anthropic permission cannot pivot to gemini); audit_scope default-denies unknown roles to SELF; OPA unreachable -> fail-closed block.

title: Phase 4: Provider Adapters
description: Concrete provider adapters dispatched by match/case in proxy/app/main.py: Anthropic (OpenAI Messages translation), Gemini (Vertex AI REST), Ollama (OpenAI-compat configurable base URL), Generic (OpenAI-compat pass-through). Shared extract_usage() for future token tracking. No LiteLLM dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Anthropic adapter round-trips OpenAI-format requests; Ollama adapter calls local Ollama; unknown provider string -> 400 (match default); each adapter supports stream=true; uv tree confirms no LiteLLM transitive dep; pytest proxy/tests/test_adapters.py passes.
close_reason: Phase 4 complete: 4 provider adapters (anthropic/gemini/ollama/generic) + extract_usage + match dispatch + 28 adapter tests. Phase 3 review applied 8 fixes (SSRF, streaming dead-code, Gemini header auth, etc.). 53/53 tests pass, lint clean. Follow-ups filed: ai-gateway-7zu, ai-gateway-0xz, ai-gateway-3gq, ai-gateway-gj3.

title: fix(correctness): pii_headers uses title-case keys inconsistently with rate-limit lowercase keys
description: proxy/app/headers.py: rate_limit_headers returns lowercase keys (x-ratelimit-...) but pii_headers returns title-case keys (X-Gateway-Pii-Redacted). HTTP headers are case-insensitive but the inconsistency is a maintenance hazard. Normalize all header key generation to lowercase throughout headers.py.

title: fix(docs): README uses change-me-in-production placeholder secrets
description: README.md quickstart section documents JWT_SECRET='change-me-in-production' and similar placeholders. Developers copying these forget to replace them. Fix: replace with random-generation shell commands: export JWT_SECRET=$(python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"). Add startup assertion in config.py rejecting known-bad placeholder values.

title: fix(config): hardcoded weak DB credentials in docker-compose.yml
description: docker-compose.yml:4-6 hardcodes POSTGRES_PASSWORD: gateway. The migrate service hardcodes the full DSN. Fix: use POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-gateway} pattern with a .env file for local dev. The migrate service should use DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL} consistently with other services.

title: fix(mock): _match_scenario raises StopIteration if clean_request scenario is missing
description: proxy/app/providers/mock.py:16: next(s for s in ALL_SCENARIOS if s.name == 'clean_request') raises StopIteration (propagates as unhandled exception) if clean_request is ever removed or renamed. Fix: use next(..., None) with an explicit fallback or assert that ALL_SCENARIOS[0].name == 'clean_request'.

title: fix(mock): rate_limit_exceed mock scenario is unreachable — decision=allow but expected_status=429
description: proxy/app/providers/mock.py: the rate_limit_exceed MockScenario has decision='allow' but expected_status=429. The mock provider only returns errors when decision=='block', so this scenario always produces a 200 with empty content, never a 429. Fix the scenario to use decision='block' or remove expected_status field if it is unused.

title: fix(test): dead roles parameter in _setup_app_state
description: proxy/tests/conftest.py:89: _setup_app_state accepts a roles parameter that is never used inside the function body. This misleads readers into thinking roles can be configured this way. Either remove the parameter or actually use it to configure the mock caller context.

title: fix(perf): audit_export fetchall() materializes full result set before streaming
description: governance/app/main.py:197: result.fetchall() materializes up to 1000 rows in memory before the first byte is yielded. Defeats the purpose of StreamingResponse. Fix: use cursor-based streaming with async iteration over the SQLAlchemy result set instead of fetchall(). Also add exception handling in the proxy generator (_stream) for upstream disconnects.

title: fix(config): governance CORS origins hardcoded to localhost only
description: governance/app/main.py:40-49: CORS origins are hardcoded to ['http://localhost:3000', 'http://localhost:8000']. Unlike the proxy which reads settings.cors_origins, governance is not configurable. Add cors_origins to governance/app/settings.py and consume it in the CORSMiddleware, consistent with proxy pattern.

title: fix(ratelimit): rate_limit remaining header always shows limit-1 instead of actual count
description: proxy/app/rate_limit.py: remaining is always max(0, limit-1) on an allowed request regardless of actual consumption. The Lua script only returns {1,0} on success without exposing the actual count. Fix: modify the Lua script to return the actual remaining count, and update RateLimitResult accordingly.

title: fix(correctness): _extract_user_message empty string causes falsy redacted_text check in pipeline
description: proxy/app/main.py:164-175: returns '' for system-only prompts. governance/app/pipeline.py:22: 'ctx.redacted_text or ctx.text' uses falsy check not None check — empty redacted text falls through to original text incorrectly. Add guard for empty text before pipeline inspection and fix the falsy check to 'if ctx.redacted_text is not None'.

title: Wire usage.extract_usage into request flow for metering
description: Phase 4 review (code-simplicity, deferred). app/providers/usage.py exposes extract_usage(provider, body) returning UsageMetrics, but no caller invokes it. Adapter responses currently leave usage extraction to downstream consumers. Phase 5 (Spend Tracking) will wire this into the metering pipeline so each completion increments per-tenant token counts.

title: Anthropic streaming: emit tool_use deltas as OpenAI tool_calls chunks
description: Phase 4 review (architecture-strategist, deferred). The Anthropic streaming translator only emits text_delta as content chunks. content_block_start / input_json_delta events for tool_use blocks are ignored, so clients using tools never see tool_call_delta chunks in the SSE stream. Map Anthropic tool_use streaming events to OpenAI-shape tool_call delta chunks.

title: P1: CORS + 1MB max body size middleware (both services)
description: CORSMiddleware with explicit allow_origins list (no wildcard). Custom middleware enforcing a 1MB request body cap, returning 413 before parsing the body. Required on both proxy and governance.
acceptance_criteria: Request from unlisted origin blocked; >1MB body returns 413 without buffering the full payload.

title: P1: config/{tenants,users,models}.yaml seed
description: tenants.yaml schema (id, name, allowed_models, rate_limit, pii_action, pii_redaction_notification, default_provider, contact_email). users.yaml (id, tenant_id, roles, initial_key). models.yaml (id, provider, base_url, alias_of?). Seed at minimum: one tenant, one admin, one tier1, one tier2, small model routing table including an alias.
acceptance_criteria: Files validate against the schemas in the plan; provisioner consumes them without errors; an alias_of entry resolves correctly via routing rules.

title: P2: DELETE /v1/users/{id} — GDPR erasure workflow
description: Admin-only endpoint. Sets deleted_at on user_pseudonym_map, overwrites real_user_id with sentinel '[ERASED]', INSERTs erasure_log row with audit_row_count from a COUNT(*) over the user's pseudonym. Returns 202 with erasure_id. Exact timestamps preserved in audit_log (hour-bucketing was rejected in the data-integrity review).
acceptance_criteria: Post-erasure: pseudonym still appears in audit_log; user_pseudonym_map row shows [ERASED]; erasure_log has matching row with correct audit_row_count.

title: P2: governance/app/harm.py — llm-guard scanners as plain function
description: harm_scan(text) -> HarmResult using llm-guard PromptInjectionScanner + BanTopicsScanner. Plain function — no HarmClassifier ABC, no registry (YAGNI per code-simplicity-reviewer).
acceptance_criteria: Jailbreak prompt yields high score; benign prompt yields low score; threshold check happens in pipeline, not in scanner.

title: P5: authz_test.rego (incl. deny+allow coexistence) + make opa-test
description: Rego test suite covering all required cases. CRITICAL test: PHI + non-approved provider + tier2 user yields allow=true AND deny non-empty (pipeline must block). Also covers provider-override scoping, audit-scope mapping, unknown-role default. make opa-test runs opa test policies/.
acceptance_criteria: make opa-test green; the deny+allow coexistence test passes (asserts the dual condition); test count documented in README.

title: P3: proxy/app/bootstrap.py — first-startup admin gated by bootstrap_state
description: On startup, check SELECT EXISTS in bootstrap_state. If false AND GATEWAY_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN env present, run a single transaction: insert admin API key (bcrypt of token), insert bootstrap_state row, commit. Concurrency: rely on unique constraint + INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. After success, call os.environ.pop('GATEWAY_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN', None) to remove from process env (mitigates exposure in subsequent crash dumps).
acceptance_criteria: First startup creates admin; second startup is a no-op even with env still set; concurrent two-pod startup never creates two admins (verified by integration test); deleting admin row + restart does NOT re-trigger bootstrap (this was the original vulnerability fixed by bootstrap_state).

title: P5: policies/llm/authz.rego — model access + data classification (resolved provider)
description: Rego policy enforcing model tier RBAC and data-classification-to-provider compliance. Evaluates against input.request.provider which is the RESOLVED provider (set by proxy.routing before /inspect). Branches on input.phase.
acceptance_criteria: PHI + non-approved provider -> deny non-empty; tier2 model + non-tier2 user -> deny; allow path returns true with empty deny for compliant requests.
close_reason: policy files committed and merged to main

title: P2: context.py + pipeline.py — PipelineContext + PII-before-OPA ordering
description: PipelineContext dataclass holds text, pii_findings, data_classification, redacted_text, harm_score, decision, violations, audit_id. pipeline.run(ctx) executes ordered stages: [pii_stage, harm_opa_stage]. PII must complete first (provides data_classification for OPA); harm and OPA run concurrently via asyncio.gather. This is the load-bearing ordering fix from the architecture/perf/backend review.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test confirms data_classification produced by pii_stage is visible to OPA input; concurrent execution of harm + OPA verified via timing assertion.

title: P3: proxy/app/headers.py — rate-limit, PII-redaction, error envelope builders
description: Helpers that produce: x-ratelimit-limit-requests / x-ratelimit-remaining-requests / x-ratelimit-reset-requests on every response (200 and 429); Retry-After (int seconds) + retry-after-ms on 429; X-Gateway-Pii-Redacted + X-Gateway-Pii-Types (types only) when redaction occurred AND tenant pii_redaction_notification != 'silent'. Error envelope builder producing the OpenAI-shape JSON with violations[], required_roles, approved_providers_for_classification (only on classification-mismatch). Never echo current_roles; never include matched substrings or offsets in any header or body.
acceptance_criteria: Header set unit tests assert presence/absence per scenario; required_roles present on policy_violation; current_roles never present in any error body; silent-tenant test confirms PII headers suppressed.

title: P3: proxy/app/auth.py — bcrypt + TTLCache + JWT HS256 pinned
description: API key validation via bcrypt against (prefix, hash) rows (never plaintext compare). cachetools.TTLCache (60s, maxsize=1000) wraps the DB lookup. JWT validated with algorithms=['HS256'] pinned — 'none' algorithm rejected. Both paths resolve to a flat CallerContext dataclass with user_id, tenant_id, roles.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid key -> 401; expired JWT -> 401; jwt.decode call refuses alg=none; second request within 60s uses cache (no Postgres round-trip, verified by counter).

title: P3: proxy/app/routing.py — 5-step provider resolution BEFORE /inspect
description: Order: (1) X-Gateway-Provider header gated by per-provider permission gateway:provider_override:<provider>; (2) models.yaml explicit entry; (3) prefix inference (gpt-*/o1-*/o3-*/o4-* -> openai; claude-* -> anthropic; gemini-* -> gemini; llama-*/mistral-*/phi-*/qwen-* -> ollama); (4) tenant default_provider; (5) 400 model_not_found (OpenAI shape). Resolution happens in the proxy entry-point so the RESOLVED provider goes into InspectRequest (security review fix).
acceptance_criteria: X-Gateway-Provider with matching permission -> override applied; without matching permission -> ignored AND audit row emitted with routing_method=override_denied; OPA evaluates the resolved provider (verified by phi-to-anthropic test); routing_method never leaks to the response body.

title: P1: scripts/pre-commit-security.sh
description: Pre-commit hook that blocks commits containing likely secrets (AWS-style keys, sk- prefixes, bearer tokens, .envrc additions). Wired via .git/hooks/pre-commit or pre-commit framework.
acceptance_criteria: Attempting to commit a file with a hardcoded sk-... key fails the hook; legitimate code commits pass.

title: P5: policies/llm/provider_override.rego — per-provider permission check
description: Checks gateway:provider_override:<provider_name> in user's permissions. Permission for anthropic does NOT imply permission for gemini (no global override).
acceptance_criteria: User with override:anthropic + header X-Gateway-Provider: gemini -> permission denied; routing layer treats as override_denied.
close_reason: policy files committed and merged to main

title: P1: Monorepo layout + docker-compose.yml with healthcheck chain
description: Create top-level directories proxy/, governance/, policies/, config/, scripts/, tests/, docs/. Author docker-compose.yml with services: postgres (5432 internal), redis (6379 internal), opa (8181 internal, openpolicyagent/opa:latest-static, --watch /policies), migrate (one-shot, depends_on postgres healthy), governance (depends_on migrate service_completed_successfully + opa healthy, start_period: 30s for Presidio warmup), proxy (depends_on redis healthy + governance healthy). All healthchecks use curl -sf.
acceptance_criteria: docker compose up -d brings every service to healthy; migrate runs before governance; OPA hot-reloads on .rego changes; governance start_period absorbs spaCy load without container kill.

Exercises the full middleware stack (auth, rate limit, governance, audit) — respx-style transport interception is unsuitable.
acceptance_criteria: make demo passes all 6 scenarios with MOCK_PROVIDERS=true and no network; streaming mock produces visible token-by-token output when delay=15ms.

title: P2: Alembic 001 initial schema (audit_log + 4 supporting tables, RLS, partitions)
description: Single migration creates: user_pseudonym_map (pseudonym PK; tenant_id REQUIRED; unique on (real_user_id, tenant_id, rotation_id)), erasure_log, partition_archive_state, bootstrap_state (singleton via CHECK id=1), audit_log (UUIDv7 audit_id, user_id stores pseudonym, routing_method column, RANGE PARTITION BY created_at). CRITICAL: pre-create first 3 monthly partitions or all INSERTs fail. REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE from gateway_app, GRANT INSERT+SELECT. ENABLE + FORCE RLS with positive-match audit_read policy. Append-only trigger raising on UPDATE/DELETE.
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies cleanly to empty DB; 3 partitions exist; gateway_app role cannot UPDATE/DELETE; mutation trigger fires; RLS denies SELECT when no session vars set.

title: P4: GenericAdapter — OpenAI-compatible pass-through
description: Pass-through adapter for any OpenAI-compatible provider configured via models.yaml base_url. Match/case default branch.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown provider routed to generic when base_url is configured; truly unknown provider returns 400.

title: P1: scripts/provision.py — IaC reconciler (idempotent)
description: Parses config/*.yaml, hashes initial keys (bcrypt with prefix), upserts API key rows, emits policies/data/users.json + policies/data/tenants.json for OPA. Prints generated keys once to stdout with 'store this now, will not be shown again' warning. Idempotent: second run prints 'no changes'.
acceptance_criteria: First run creates rows and prints keys; second run is a no-op; OPA --watch picks up the emitted data documents within seconds.

title: P4: OllamaAdapter — OpenAI-compat with configurable base URL
description: Ollama exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; adapter simply rewrites base URL from models.yaml or tenant config. Used as the realistic local-LLM path in demos.
acceptance_criteria: Local Ollama serving llama3 responds via the proxy with the same request shape as OpenAI.

title: P1: Base FastAPI apps with lifespan + /health
description: proxy/app/main.py and governance/app/main.py: FastAPI() with lifespan context manager. GET /health returns 503 until all dependencies are ready (governance: Presidio initialized; proxy: Redis + governance reachable). Governance /health also queries partition_archive_state for stuck partitions (detached_at > 48h AND dumped_at IS NULL) and surfaces 'degraded' in that case.
acceptance_criteria: /health flips 503 -> 200 once lifespan completes; governance reports degraded when a synthetic stuck partition row is inserted.

title: P3: proxy/app/governance_client.py — /inspect caller with X-Internal-Token + tenacity
description: HTTPX async client posting to governance:8742/inspect. Always sends X-Internal-Token (loaded once at startup via secrets module). Sends the RESOLVED provider in the request body. Tenacity retry (3 attempts, exponential backoff). Fail-closed: any unrecoverable error or non-200 -> raise an exception that the route handler converts to 503 (block, do NOT forward to provider).
acceptance_criteria: Governance down -> proxy returns 503 with zero upstream calls; transient 5xx -> retried then succeeds; X-Internal-Token header present on every call.

title: P2: governance/app/pii.py — Presidio singleton, asyncio.to_thread, init lock
description: Module-level AnalyzerEngine + AnonymizerEngine. initialize() guarded by asyncio.Lock to prevent concurrent re-init. Both engines constructed via asyncio.to_thread (both are CPU-bound at construction, per kieran-python-reviewer). scan() and redact() also use asyncio.to_thread. Never use deprecated get_event_loop().
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent initialize under concurrent startup (lock works); /inspect under load does not block the event loop; pyright clean.

title: P3: proxy/app/config.py — Settings + mock_mode resolved once at startup
description: Pydantic Settings reading all env vars. mock_mode resolution: MOCK_PROVIDERS=true takes precedence over OPENAI_API_KEY=mock sentinel. Resolved once into settings.mock_mode; never re-read per request.
acceptance_criteria: MOCK_PROVIDERS=true forces mock even with real OPENAI_API_KEY; OPENAI_API_KEY=mock alone enables mock mode; mock_mode value is stable across requests.

title: P5: policies/llm/allow_model.rego — enumerate-and-filter
description: Single-model allow query used by /v1/me and /v1/models filtering. Intentionally NOT partial evaluation — loop of HTTP OPA queries against allow_model per model is simple, correct on every policy change, and avoids residual-policy complexity. Tenant allowed_models is bounded (~20).
acceptance_criteria: Loop of N opa.evaluate calls returns the correct allowed subset; results match the rego ground truth for a fixture user.
close_reason: policy files committed and merged to main

title: P2: governance/app/retention.py — detach-dump-drop coordinator + drift check
description: Coordinator that (1) creates next month's partition if missing, (2) walks partition_archive_state advancing rows: detach -> dump-to-S3 -> verify -> drop, (3) handles recovery by querying 'dumped_at IS NULL AND detached_at < now() - interval 1 hour'. /health sub-check surfaces 'degraded' if any partition is detached >48h without dump.
acceptance_criteria: Forcing a stuck row makes /health degraded; full happy-path advances a synthetic old partition through all four states.

title: P2: GET /v1/audit + /v1/audit/export (keyset-paginated JSONL)
description: GET /v1/audit/export?format=jsonl&after_created_at=<ts>&after_audit_id=<uuid>&until=<ts>. SQL: WHERE (created_at, audit_id) > ($1,$2) AND created_at <= $3 ORDER BY created_at, audit_id LIMIT 500. created_at upper bound mandatory for partition pruning. UUIDv7 audit_id makes ordering align with created_at to millisecond precision. Response: Content-Type application/x-ndjson, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Link: <…>; rel="next" carrying the keyset of the last emitted row.
acceptance_criteria: Stream completes for >10k rows without server-side cursor; Link header round-trips correctly; only the targeted partitions are scanned (verified by EXPLAIN ANALYZE).

title: P2: governance/app/audit.py — metadata-only write_audit() with written_at
description: write_audit() coroutine called from FastAPI BackgroundTasks. Stores pii_findings as JSONB list of {type, start, end, score} — NEVER matched substrings or prompt content. Populates written_at separately from created_at (lets us detect write lag). user_id column receives the HMAC pseudonym, never the raw identifier. routing_method always set.
acceptance_criteria: SQL test asserts audit_log.user_id is pseudonym; pii_findings JSONB never contains matched_text key; written_at populated and distinct from created_at; BackgroundTasks failure logs to stderr but never crashes the request.

title: P4: GeminiAdapter — Vertex AI REST
description: Translates to Gemini REST API. Handles auth via service account or API key; response re-shaped to OpenAI envelope.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end request with model=gemini-* succeeds; streaming supported.

title: P3: proxy/app/rate_limit.py — Redis Lua sliding window with retry_after return
description: Lua script: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE (evict stale) + ZADD using an INCR counter for unique member IDs (math.random() produces duplicates per kieran-python-reviewer) + ZCOUNT + unconditional EXPIRE (must run even on deny path). Returns {allowed: 0|1, retry_after_seconds: int}. EVALSHA at startup. Keyed on user_id from CallerContext (not on headers).
acceptance_criteria: 20 concurrent requests at limit=10 -> exactly 10 succeed (atomic, no over-admit); 429 includes correct Retry-After; EXPIRE observed on both allow and deny paths (no key leak).

title: P2: governance/app/db.py — AsyncEngine + connection checkout listener
description: SQLAlchemy AsyncEngine over asyncpg. Register a sync_engine 'checkout' event listener that RESETs app.current_user_id, app.current_tenant_id, app.current_scope on every connection acquisition BEFORE OPA-derived values are set. Mandatory to prevent session-var leak across pooled connections (security review).
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent test with two different scopes proves session vars from prior request do not leak; RESET observed in pg_stat statements.

title: P4: AnthropicAdapter — OpenAI Messages translation + streaming
description: Translates OpenAI chat/completions format to Anthropic Messages API (system prompt extraction, role mapping, tool_use translation). Streaming via aiter_bytes; response re-shaped back to OpenAI envelope so SDK clients are unaware of the upstream.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end request through proxy with model=claude-3-5-sonnet round-trips; streaming chunks delivered; SDK parses response without errors.

OPA: shared-cpu-1x (256MB). auto_stop_machines=true on proxy + governance. fly secrets set: JWT_SECRET, GOVERNANCE_INTERNAL_TOKEN, GATEWAY_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN, PSEUDONYM_HMAC_KEY, all provider keys, DATABASE_URL (internal Fly Postgres). [env]: OPA_URL=http://opa.internal:8181, LOG_LEVEL=info, DOCS_ENABLED=false.

description: HTTPX async client calling OPA /v1/data/llm/authz with 50ms timeout. Block if allow=false OR len(deny)>0 (deny wins even when allow fires). Explicit exception classes — never bare 'except Exception'. Fail-closed on TimeoutException, ConnectError, missing result key.

title: Sanitize upstream error bodies before forwarding to clients
description: Phase 4 review (security-sentinel, deferred). When an upstream returns a non-200, adapters pass the raw upstream body and content-type through. This can leak provider-specific internal error details (request IDs, internal hostnames, stack traces). Translate upstream errors into a normalized OpenAI-shape error envelope, log the original upstream body server-side for debugging.

title: Generic adapter: per-base_url client pooling
description: Phase 4 review (performance-oracle, deferred). The generic adapter currently shares one global httpx.AsyncClient with no base_url and constructs the absolute URL per request. This works but loses keepalive benefits when many requests target the same base_url. Pool clients by base_url so connections to common third-party endpoints are reused.
